Products, prices, SKU, stock and fulfillment sources are independent per store, and a copy between countries never shares stock. C-05 and C-13 test the stock half; the copy-to-country tool (deferred, #76 G9) and the SKU rules (#72, #76) belong to the catalogue unit.

cross_axis_notes.text: Product eligibility for shipping, export, import and regulated health goods; the system must not assume every product ships across borders. D2-06 consumes the result for method eligibility.
The setting that allows cross-border selling, courier route support, and shipping cost, tax and duties for cross-border orders.
The tax and regulatory-constraint parts of the payment-case analysis (local and international) depend on the tax and regulatory units; D2-18 only pins the payment path.
Acceptance of the customer's address for a cross-border destination.
The destination country does not change the stock owner or the selling company; D2-07 and D2-15 rely on that.

One store and one company per checkout, local prices, and the order snapshot of company, currency, tax, prices, address and fulfilment source, including refunds in the original currency and merchant account. D2-07, D2-10 and D2-15 need the snapshot; GCC-05 slice 2 (order currency record) sits on branch gcc/p1-storefront-currency with no pull request.
Each country's legal company owns its payment gateways and bank accounts; the legal entity model (Q-10) is the key D2-07 needs.

Pausing a store must not lose earlier orders or stop webhooks, refunds and settlements. The payment half is D2-14 (switched-off storefront still finishes payments; due payments and status stay open); the rest belongs to store operations.
Wallet top-up through a gateway (add_fund_to_wallet hook), wallet debits at checkout and refunds credited to the wallet; wallet chain PR 9 to PR 14 and PR 34 to PR 36.
Staff scope on payment screens: PR 77 and PR 82 scope the refund and order lists, but gateway settings, MyFatoorah screens and refund execution are not scoped (the integrations slice is not built).
The sale gate that refuses new payments in a storefront without approved legal texts (PR 42, PR 49, GCC-11) belongs to legal policies; D2-05 only adds gateway eligibility to the same seam.
Customer and admin notices for payment success, failure, pending and refund outcomes, and alerts on mismatches.
Gateway fees, settlements and the posting of payments and refunds to accounting or Odoo per company; PaymentFeeContributor and Odoo reconciliation sit there.
Payment and webhook monitoring (PaymentsPanel, integration health) and the GCC-20 payment incidents view for the platform owner; the platform admin API has no payment data yet.
The regression plan item on payments, refunds and webhooks (line 669) draws on D2-02, D2-11 to D2-16 and D2-18.

cross_axis_notes.text: The same customer's order history across countries (with permissions) is a customer-account feature, not a wallet one. E-04 only needs statements to stay per market even where order history is shared.

A local manager must not see other countries' customer transactions. E-04 holds the wallet and loyalty part: PR 82 leaves customer wallet and loyalty reports and the wallet bonus tab un-narrowed (GCC-14c decision 15). Admin add-fund sits behind module:people (D21).

cross_axis_notes.belongs_to_unit: customer accounts, address, coupons and legal units (plan 345-357, 420-428, 393-403)
cross_axis_notes.text: Axis G also lists login, OAuth/OTP, accounts, vouchers (coupons), addresses, orders, consents and privacy. Only wallets, points and balance preservation are in unit E (E-01, E-02, E-06, E-07).
Orders record neither market nor currency (GCC-20 API doc: order_currency_not_recorded). E-01, E-05, E-16 and E-17 need it before a wallet or ledger row can carry a currency.

A wallet top-up credits through add_fund_to_wallet_success with no wallet-level idempotency; only some gateways guard the hook (Paymera, MtnCash). Gateway replay guard and per-entity gateway accounts belong to D2; PR 56 (settlement for the named payer) is D2 work with a small referral effect (E-15).
Wallet and loyalty terms (stored value, expiry, refund to wallet, retention after account deletion) need approved per-entity texts; E-01 and E-08 name the legal review.

odoo_reconciliations on main already holds per (seller, Odoo company, channel, period, currency) source, ledger and Odoo amounts. Posting of wallet top-up liabilities and the add-fund bonus to Odoo is not coded; E-17 depends on the company mapping.

Report 06 (reconcile balances, orders, payments), Report 08 (mixing of money and balances) and Report 10 (carts, wallets, loyalty tests) lie outside the unit ranges; their wallet and loyalty parts are E-06, E-07 and the next tasks of E-01 and E-03.
Who may trigger wallet-paying actions (due payments, refunds, order status) is covered by the ownership PRs 16, 20, 21, 22, 23, 27; E-10 and E-13 assume them and are not tested together with them.

coverage_gaps: No production, staging or backup data was inspected (charter section 4): real wallet and loyalty balances, the storage unit (currency_model, E04-F02), ledger-versus-balance drift and legacy customer_wallets rows are UNVERIFIED.

No tree and no CI run holds the money chain together: PRs 6, 9-15, 25 and 29-36 are in neither PR 75 nor PR 83 (only PR 55 and 56 are in PR 75). Conflicts among them and with the security and GCC sets come from file overlap only; git merge-tree was not run (read-only rule).

CI was read as job conclusions (ci-table, ci json), not logs: a concurrency test skipped inside a green job cannot be excluded for heads without PR 14's engine guard; local MySQL numbers are from PR bodies.

Delivery-man wallets and cash collection, the admin wallet's other writers, seller and admin earning credits (OrderManager wallet_manage_on_order_status_change) and add-fund bonus tiers were read only as far as needed; no PR in this unit changes them.

Marketplace ledger tables (vendor_ledger_entries, vendor_settlements, vendor_payout_requests) are not defined in database/migrations, so their schema is UNVERIFIED in the repository; no test reads them.
The restricted security annex (SEC-E04-xx) was not read; permission gates of wallet routes (D21, D22) and mass-assignment exposure of the fillable wallet columns were not exercised.
Flutter apps were read, not run: the missing Idempotency-Key is a source search over seven seller-app refs; the customer app's wallet screens were not opened on a device.

cross_axis_notes.text: The admin product tools (a product's country chosen once, shown and filtered; the bulk-import country) are B-08. G-03 covers only the staff scope on the same screens; both use PRs 64 and 74.

The platform admin API, its MFA, sessions, hash-chained audit trail and the step-up primitive belong to L (L-01 to L-05, L-12, L-15). G-13 owns only the intersection with the staff scope (PR 84); G-14 needs the step-up primitive of L-15.

Storefront context in jobs, queue payloads and scheduled tasks is A1-14. G-11 needs the same context design plus the staff actor; whether queued mail, push and exports render per market is A1's owner question.

An order's stored market, currency and legal entity (D1-03, D1-06) would replace the line-based attribution that G-04 and G-05 use and settle the mixed-country and unattributed-order policy; money by entity belongs to D1.
Wallet and loyalty per store, company and currency (E-01, E-02, E-17) must exist before G-07 can scope a customer's wallet data by country; the ledgers and their readers belong to E.
Per-company gateway accounts and secrets (D2-07, D2-08) own the storage side; G-16 covers who may read or change them in the panel and the masking of the legacy gateway form.
Channel and Odoo secret protection is H2-15 (MERGED); G-16 only references it and adds the panel-wide view of secrets.
The customer's own cross-country order history and the privacy rules are A2-10 and A2-15; G-07 is the staff-side counterpart and shares the legal review of what a local manager may see.
Stock ownership per storefront and the owner of inventory locations, pools and warehouses (C-05) must exist before G-08 can scope the warehouse and channel stock screens.
Store activation and the pause modes (GCC-12; I2-11 to I2-16) are sensitive actions whose scoping, confirmation and audit G-14 has to cover once they exist.
Theme content and publishing per storefront are F; the theme editor permissions (ThemePermissionService) and the theme builder pickers are slice 4 of the staff scope (G-09).

Vendor-panel and seller-API staff (seller_staff) are another principal with their own tables and permissions; no staff country scope applies to them until sellers have markets. Seller-side permissions belong to K; G does not scope them.

The combined security and GCC tree (PR 75 with PR 83) does not exist. It decides whether G-03 to G-06 can leave IMPLEMENTED IN DRAFT and whether the gate PRs keep passing StaffScopeDocTest; it belongs to the integration and tests units.

coverage_gaps: Nothing was run. The assessment read code, tests and PR bodies. Counts and timings quoted from PR bodies (counter cost 1.4 s on 60k orders, mutation passes, test totals) are pr-body claims; CI states come from ci-table.md and the ci JSON (latest attempt, read 2026-11-18).

No tree holds the security set (PR 75) and the GCC chain (PR 83). The expected failure of StaffScopeDocTest::test_the_doc_carries_the_permission_each_covered_route_asks_for after #67 and #73 (the dashboard widget and invoice rows say none in the doc) is inferred from reading the test and the doc, not shown by a run.

Test bodies were read only where they decide an acceptance criterion (names everywhere, a few bodies); the StaffScope, security and platform tests were not read in full and the mutation-pass claims of the PR bodies are unverified.

Production and live data are UNVERIFIED: the live roles' module_access, the admins table shape, whether audit_logs exists on the live database (no migration creates it and the installation dump is not in the repository), the live application key and the live app versions.
The real admin Blade pages (layout, dashboard, order, POS, product, customer, vendor) are rendered by no test (stub views stand in); whether they render for a restricted employee is not shown.

Slices 4 to 6 were read only as survey tables and guard entries; the code of those controllers, the employee and role views, the monitoring panel and the developer console were not inspected in depth.
MariaDB 11.4.2 ran the StaffScope tests only in the CI-only integration #83; the module-gate tests ran on MariaDB in each pull request's own Fulfillment + security job.
Vendor panel, seller API staff, the seller app and the platform admin mobile app were not assessed (units K and L); the customer app has no staff-permission surface.

cross_axis_notes.text: Refund processing, payment-gateway callbacks and webhooks (MyFatoorah, Paymob) that must keep working for a stopped storefront are payment code. I2-16 only pins that they carry no sale gate and that a started payment finishes in its storefront; per-gateway behaviour and refund tests belong to the payments unit.

Settlements and ledgers of a stopped storefront (seller payouts, marketplace settlement, wallet, loyalty) are financial-record code. They are not narrowed by storefront today and need their own stop test; I2-16 only records the gap.

Shipment sync and provider webhooks (Torod, M5AZN, DeliverySyria) must continue for a stopped storefront. They are queue and webhook code outside the sale gate; the shipping unit owns the per-provider test.

Marketplace channel orders and webhooks (Amazon, Noon, Trendyol) and Odoo posting are neither gated nor narrowed by storefront; whether they are storefront sales is an owner decision (I2-03). The marketplace unit owns their behaviour after a stop.

The marketing consent register (no consent record for e-mail, SMS, WhatsApp or push, Discovery E06-F09) and campaign audience isolation belong to I1. I2-07 covers only legal-document acceptance receipts.

Maintenance and pause push topics (maintenance_mode_start_user_app and others) are global today. A per-storefront Maintenance mode, and the plan rule that necessary order notifications continue after a stop (line 412), need market-scoped topics and templates from the notifications unit.

The customer-app screens that show legal pages (html_screen_view, checkout_condition_checkbox) must pass the storefront once I2-08 exists. The browse-only notice and the sale guard of lavkooapp PR 3 and 5 are counted in I2-04; the storefront chooser and caches (lavkooapp PR 6, 7) belong to J.
The seller app reads the same global business pages and has no sellable or readiness handling; per-country seller terms and a seller-side stop notice belong to the seller-app unit (I2-08, I2-03).

Switching a storefront to Active, Browse Only, Maintenance or Redirect from the mobile Super Admin is GCC-20 level 3 and needs separate owner authorization and security review. The read-only markets and the legal_not_ready alert (lavkoo PR 71) are counted in I2-11 only.

The legal entity recorded on a receipt is one global GCC_LEGAL_ENTITY value; legal entities per storefront and customer-level consent scopes (registration and seller-registration checkboxes) belong to the entity and customer-identity units.

Readiness inputs the preflight (I2-11) must read, such as a payment account per legal entity and currency, belong to the payments unit; theme publication (F), the currency decision GCC-05 and catalogue presence (B) belong to their units.

coverage_gaps: Production content of business_pages and the live server legal pages (slugs, status, languages, last edit): not inspected, no production read is authorized by the charter. UNVERIFIED.

No CI-proven combined tree of the security set (PR 75) and the GCC chain (PR 83) is in the data pack. routes/web/routes.php, routes/rest_api/v1/api.php, resources/lang/*/messages.php and app/Utils/module-helper.php are touched by both, so I2-02, I2-04 and I2-16 are capped below INTEGRATED AND TESTED.

Refs pushed after the CI table was read (04:58 UTC): gcc/release/security-gcc-integration-ci (f6fb03af) and gcc/release/all-integration-ci (55487514) contain both sets, with the sale gate, PR 40 fix and legal tests intact. No CI result for them is in the data pack, so the cap stays; re-read once their runs are green.

Draft PR 87 (gcc/p1-storefront-currency, 4af1c305) is not in the PR index or CI table. It makes StorefrontSellingGate and StorefrontListing also require the storefront currency (GCC-05) and changes constructor signatures that I2-02, I2-04 and I2-11 rely on; not assessed.

The legal tests on the heads of lavkoo PR 38, 39, 42 and 43 ran on SQLite only (their CI has no storefront group on MySQL or MariaDB). A database-specific pass is claimed only on PR 49 head b52d9b2 and PR 83 head 8ff3410, where the Storefront tests jobs exist.
The Deployment overlay job is red on every lavkoo head because the server baseline is 395 commits behind main. Recorded here as a known deployment-tooling result, not counted as a test failure.

The customer app screens (cart, checkout) and the flag-on build were never rendered or run on a device or emulator, and the app was never run against the backend; only analyzer, unit and widget tests in CI were read.
The seller app (lavkooappseller) was only searched for sellable, browse-only, legal and business-pages handling; nothing was found and its market scope was not assessed here.

The Auction module directory is absent from the checkout, so its order entry points (sale-gate coverage) could not be listed. Only the default theme exists in this tree; e-mail templates that link to legal pages were noted, not traced one by one.

Settlement, shipment, webhook and support continuity for a stopped storefront was inferred from routes and the runbook (not gated, not narrowed by storefront); no test or run exists, and those code areas belong to other units.

Arabic wording of the refusal message, the app notice and any legal text was not reviewed by a native Arabic reviewer, and the legal substance of the document types and locales is unreviewed by a qualified legal reviewer.

cross_axis_notes.text: Admin, AdminRole, module_access and the admin-panel country scopes (GCC-14c slices) are owned by the admin-panel unit; K-03 and K-08 cover only the seller and seller-staff principal.

The general manager who sees every country is the platform principal of GCC-20 (separate API, MFA, sessions, shell in app#4 and #6); K-11 and K-13 only require that seller sign-in, token and gate stay untouched by it.
Market-scoped push topics, order notifications built from the store that created the order and consent rules are owned by the notifications unit (I1-05, I1-06); K-10 is the app side.
The order market, currency, tax and address snapshot (GCC-05) that K-04 and K-09 need is owned by the orders unit (D1-06).
The seller wallet, withdrawals and the ledger by legal entity and currency (E-12, E-17) are owned by the wallet unit; K-09 only presents them per market.
Seller products belonging to a market (B-09) and SKU and barcode uniqueness per country (B-04, B-05) are owned by the catalog unit; K-04 and K-05 are the seller app side.
Stock ownership per storefront and inventory locations (C-05) are owned by the inventory unit; the seller app's warehouse and stock screens (K-04) read that model.
The per-country theme engine, theme cache and brand overrides are owned by the themes unit; K-17 only keeps the seller app apart from them.
Store context in seller APIs (A1-11) and market-scoped app caches (A1-16) are owned by the foundation unit; K-01 and K-02 are the seller app side.

The sale gate on POS, seller API and marketplace order writers for a storefront that may not sell (I2-09) and the stop modes are owned by the policies unit; the seller app has no sellable or paused-market handling yet.
The customer app already builds the storefront chooser, header refresh and cache hygiene (J-02, J-03, J-04); K-02 should reuse its pattern instead of inventing another.
The combined security + GCC tree (M1-03) is needed before any seller criterion that depends on both sets can be shown to pass together.

cross_axis_notes.text: Storefront context in jobs, queue payloads, scheduled tasks, caches and notifications (A1-14, A1-15, A1-17) is built by the base unit; M2-02 and M2-18 only test it.
Staff scope slices 4-6, legal-entity scopes and action scopes (G-09, G-12) belong to the admin and staff unit; M2-03 tracks the tests of slices 1-3 and of the combined tree.
Phone and e-mail identity matching, consents by storefront and order history across markets (A2-06, A2-10, A2-13) belong to the customer unit; M2-04 tracks the cross-storefront account tests.

Per-storefront wallet and loyalty accounts, reconciliation of historical balances and migration of Saudi balances (E-01 to E-04, E-06, E-07) belong to the wallets unit; M2-05 and M2-17 track tests only.
The legal-entity checkout model, order tax and currency snapshots and the multi-vendor split (D1-06, D1-07, D1-12) belong to the orders unit; M2-06 tracks the tests.

The storefront currency seam, local price display and the money of admin product screens (GCC-05; B-02, B-03, D1-06) belong to the catalogue and orders units; M2-07 tracks the tests and the missing slice 5.
Country-specific providers, pools and the fulfillment source per product per storefront (C-01 and following) belong to the inventory unit; M2-08 tracks the race tests only.
The cross-border eligibility engine, carrier routes and the regulated-goods rule (H1-01 to H1-06) belong to the shipping unit; M2-09 records that no code or test exists.

Per-country theme drafts, publish, preview and rollback (F-01, F-02, F-07, F-08) belong to the themes unit; J (J-04, J-06) and K (K-01 to K-03) own the app caches and the market scope; M2-10 tracks the tests.
Gateway accounts, secrets, webhooks and reconciliation per entity and market (D2-07 to D2-10, D2-16) belong to the payments unit; M2-11 tracks the tests.
A channel account country and legal entity, per-market channel rules and Odoo per entity (H2-06, H2-07, H2-10) belong to the integrations unit; M2-12 tracks the tests.

Legal text authoring and approval, stop modes Browse Only, Maintenance and Redirect, and the checkout wiring of acceptance receipts (I2-01 to I2-05, I2-13 to I2-16) belong to the policies unit; M2-13 and M2-14 track the tests.
Notification templates, audiences, push topics and consent (I1-03 to I1-09) belong to the notifications unit; M2-13 records that no market-scoped notification test exists.

Engineering safety rules as release discipline and the Saudi baseline unchanged while switches are off (M1-17, M1-18) are also tracked by the security and deployment unit; M2-16 and M2-01 track them in migrations, CI and tests.
The Report 06 and Report 10 documents themselves (presence, language, evidence rules: M3-06, M3-10) belong to the reports unit; M2 measures what the plan says to build and test.
Per-market monitoring for the platform owner (L-07, L-10, L-18) is built by the GCC-20 unit; M2-18 tests only the operational side.

Old Saudi URLs, redirects, canonical rules and country path routing (A1-05, A1-08), old product URLs (B-18) and app deep links (J-10) belong to the base, catalogue and customer-app units; M2-17 tests that old links still resolve as Saudi.

result.checked: Read-only throughout. I checked 15 requirements. All 85 evidence triples (5 to 6 per requirement) match with git grep -c -F at the stated ref and path, so there is no failing triple. I confirmed that 62 (ref, test file) pairs named in the tests entries exist at the PR head named, that the 19 branch heads cited equal the PR head shas, and that PR 45, 58, 59, 60, 62, 54 and 56 are in PR 75, PR 42, 43, 47, 48 and 53 are in PR 83, and PR 16, 21, 22 and 23 are in neither. I read the assertions of the tests behind every MET criterion and every ci test claim (about 60 methods) and recounted 11, 15, 13, 9, 17, 5, 12, 10, 19 and 20 (the 41 and 22 are PR-body counts with data providers, not recounted). I read ci/*.json and ci-table.md for each named head (all green except the known Deployment overlay), the workflow of each head to see which directories run on MySQL 8 and MariaDB (Security, Address and Storefront groups; Auth, Api, Payment, Payments and Cart only in Tests, SQLite, which runs tests/Unit and tests/Feature whole) and the cited tests for skip conditions (none). The two states at INTEGRATED AND TESTED or higher hold: A2-03's code files are not touched by the GCC chain and its tests are in PR 75 with green CI, and A2-11 is on main with pinning tests. exists_now and done_in_drafts were read against main, PR 75, PR 83 and the lavkooapp heads for 14 of 15 requirements, and each correction above was re-checked against the trees (I cross-read docs/gcc/tracker in the handoff worktree to see which findings were already applied, then verified each one myself). Plan lines 345-357 and 509-513 were re-read in Arabic: lines 351, 513 and the coupon and wallet part of 511 belong to E, and lines 354 (policy half) and 355 have no requirement in this result, so they are listed as missing although I2-05 and G-07 exist. Findings: 1 state refutation (A2-12), 3 criterion corrections (A2-05, A2-09, A2-10), 1 test claim (A2-05), 2 missing requirements and 30 field corrections; main findings are false 'no login test' and 'no destination rule' statements, the stale view of orders and migrations now that gcc/p1-storefront-currency (PR 87, 4af1c305) exists, next tasks that cannot be done as written, and an unproven 'users has no country_code'. state_refutations.why: Criterion 4 ('With the market switch off, the Saudi wallet credit, debit, balance and ledger row behave exactly as today') is rated MET (WalletLedgerCharacterizationTest at PR 6 5c4b3e6 and WalletDebitBoundaryCharacterizationTest at PR 34 832377a, CI green at both heads). The rubric says NOT STARTED means no code anywhere, and a MET or CODED criterion means code exists, so MET plus three MISSING is IN PROGRESS. Caveat: that criterion is only a baseline pin (no market switch exists on any branch, and PR 11 and PR 36 change the very behaviour the two tests pin), so if a baseline pin should not count as started, re-rate the criterion MISSING and keep NOT STARTED instead.

Criterion 3 ('wallet_balance, total_wallet_balance and total_loyalty_point keep key and meaning for the default market') is rated CODED (profile_model, wallet_transaction_model and loyalty_point_model read them), so code exists; with four MISSING criteria the rubric state is IN PROGRESS. Draft code toward the requirement also exists: PR 82 hides the admin, vendor and delivery-man wallet cards from a restricted employee, and lavkooapp#7 lists the wallet and points controllers in its inventory test. Same caveat as E-01: the CODED criterion is the unchanged legacy readers; re-rate it MISSING if that should not count.

Criterion 1 is rated CODED and it is real code, not a baseline pin: VendorLedger::record on main stamps a currency (the store's base currency), is idempotent on (seller, entry type, reference) and locks the previous entry, and SettlementEngine and PayoutService sit beside it. Code exists and four criteria are MISSING, so the rubric state is IN PROGRESS.

ac_corrections.ac_text_start: Every difference falls in a named class and zero unexplained differences
ac_corrections.why: Classes A (rows with no owner), B (rows of a deleted user), C (NULL balance), D (float residue within the tolerance), E (explained by an evidence file of user ids) and F (anything else) are counted by BalanceReconciler, and class F is a FAIL check so the command exits 1 while one user is unexplained. Tests in WalletReconcileCommandTest exist; no CI for the head in the pack.

ac_corrections.ac_text_start: Debit rows are matched to pay_by_wallet orders by reference, time and amount
ac_corrections.why: WalletPaymentMatcher matches each order_place debit to a wallet-paid order group (payment_method pay_by_wallet or wallet, grouped by COALESCE(order_group_id, id)) of the same customer within --match-tolerance 0.02 and --match-window 600 s and counts unmatched debits and unmatched groups. The key is customer, amount and time, not a reference, because the ledger holds no order id; judge whether that satisfies 'by reference'. No CI for the head in the pack.

ac_corrections.ac_text_start: The report writes nothing, prints no names or contact data and refuses to run outside
ac_corrections.why: ReadOnlyRunner locks the session read-only (SET SESSION TRANSACTION READ ONLY or PRAGMA query_only), ReadOnlyProbe::select accepts reads only, and the last check 'nothing was written' fails the run if any non-read statement was issued; the report holds counts and sums, ids only with --list-unexplained. It refuses when APP_ENV is production without --allow-production-read-only and when --expect-database differs from the connected database; it cannot tell an authorised copy from any other non-production database. No CI for the head in the pack.

ac_corrections.ac_text_start: The legacy customer_wallets and customer_wallet_histories tables are included
ac_corrections.why: BalanceReconciler::legacyTablesCheck reports whether the two legacy tables exist and their row counts and sums (balance, royality_points, transaction_amount) and warns that they are outside the comparison and must be migrated or declared frozen. They are included in the report; the command does not itself declare them frozen. No CI for the head in the pack.

state_refutations.why: All six listed criteria are MET and verified (28 test methods at PR 83 8ff3410 and PR 38 122960e, in tests/Feature/Storefront, run by the whole-suite SQLite job and by Storefront tests MySQL 8 and MariaDB 11.4.2, all green), but one criterion the requirement needs is missing from the list and is not met. StorefrontLegalReadiness::isReady() fails open on an empty configuration: it returns true after a loop over requiredPairsOf(), and requiredPairsOf() builds pairs from config gcc.storefronts.legal.required_documents x (locales_by_country.<CC> ?? required_locales). An empty required_documents, an empty required_locales or a country entry of [] yields no pair, the loop never runs, and any non-grandfathered country whose table exists is ready (app/Services/Storefront/StorefrontLegalReadiness.php lines 36-44 and 91-103 at 8ff3410). No test sets either list empty (git grep of tests finds only the locales_by_country.QA = ['ar'] override). Plan line 395 (approved documents before sales) and the requirement's own fail-closed principle (unreadable table closes the storefront) make 'a storefront with no required document type or no required locale configured is not ready' a criterion; it is MISSING. The earlier tracker iteration listed exactly this as a MISSING criterion of the readiness rule. Add it as a MISSING criterion; the state follows the rubric (some code, one criterion MISSING).

field_corrections.problem: Omits a known defect of the rule itself: isReady() fails open when required_documents, required_locales or a locales_by_country entry is empty (no pair is produced, the loop is skipped, the method returns true), and a table that exists without the effective_from column (only the first migration run) is treated as readable although the query then throws. No test covers either case.
field_corrections.replacement: 1) No code writes rows (status, approval, effective_from, revoked_at): rows exist only by hand or in tests (I2-05). 2) isReady answers a bool with no reasons (I2-11). 3) Document types, locales and effective-date rules per country are engineering defaults a qualified reviewer must confirm (I2-10). 4) Saudi texts are not in the table (SA is grandfathered in code, I2-06). 5) Fails open on an empty configuration: requiredPairsOf() builds the pairs from required_documents x the locales, so an empty document list, an empty required_locales or a locales_by_country entry of [] gives no pair and isReady() returns true for any non-grandfathered country whose table exists (StorefrontLegalReadiness.php lines 36-44 and 91-103); tableExists() checks only the table, so a table without the effective_from column makes the query throw instead of closing the storefront. No test covers either case.

field_corrections.problem: The task moves the requirement to READY FOR OWNER REVIEW, which needs no known defect, but it does not include the fail-open of an empty configuration.
field_corrections.replacement: On gcc/p1-storefront-legal-readiness (PR 38): first make StorefrontLegalReadiness fail closed when requiredPairsOf() yields no pair (an empty document list, an empty locale list or a country entry of [] means not ready) and when the table lacks effective_from, with a test for each on SQLite and the Storefront MySQL/MariaDB jobs. ac_corrections.ac_text_start: A refund decision and a return receipt happen once
ac_corrections.why: The refund half is not implemented and not proven. RefundConcurrencyTest (PR 15 59133c3) calls skipUntilOwnerDecision() (markTestSkipped) as the first line of all four tests (RF-01 simultaneous refunded statuses, RF-03 return amount, RF-04 POS cancel, IDEM-08 delivered points). The proposals file says 'Every test is skipped' and 'Nothing in this document is implemented'; RF-01 documents that two overlapping refunded updates both pay. A green job therefore proves no refund race. Only the return receipt half is proven (ReturnReceiptConcurrencyTest, PR 17 5cbc384, not skipped). Split: 'a return receipt happens once under two processes' stays MET; 'a refund decision pays once under simultaneous requests' is MISSING.
